items.title: Artie Shaw — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Had to hire a lawyer whose wife had been to school with Elizabeth Shipley.

ctx.x: What did the Un-American Activities Committee think you’d done? What did they accuse . . .?

Communist party. I joined a lot of organizations. One of the things they asked me was, would you join this and join that? I said, “Yeah. Committee for a Democratic Far- Eastern Policy. What’s wrong with that?” “Don’t you know it’s a communist front?” So then it got to the World Peace Congress. I said, “[Eugene] Ormandy was on that. Thomas Mann was on it. Einstein.” He said, “All pinkos.” I said, “I take my stand with those pinkos.” Anyway, then they said, “Don’t you know that was a communist front?” I said, “I…

there and lived there. Then I met Evelyn [Keyes]. We got married. Well, we didn’t get married. We lived together for a while, and then she wanted to get married, because it was an awkward position in those days. And that was that. Meanwhile I wrote and I fished and I breathed. I’m a devout breather. I keep advising people, don’t stop doing that. They talk about, you need water. You need air, first.
